incident-bot: ALERT: Spike in 429/timeout errors for embeddings endpoint (region-eu-west-1) — paging @taylor.g :rotating_light:
Taylor G.: joining. saw the spikes on the dashboard — looks like a cache-invalidation wave caused multiple upstream model replicas to rebuild KV caches simultaneously. Tracing showing queue saturation on the embedding workers.
Nia S.: can you confirm which customer segments are affected? Ops metrics show increased retries for both hosted and dedicated pools.
Marcus H.: preliminary: majority of 429s are from short-burst traffic patterns hitting the same prefix keys. We saw a rapid cache eviction triggered by a mis-scheduled maintenance job.
Taylor G.: mitigation step 1: enabled soft-rate-limiter and increased max concurrent requests on embedding workers to smooth the burst. Command: `infractl set-rate-limit --service embeddings --region eu-west-1 --soft 2000` (applied at 2026-03-12T09:12:41Z).
Luis M.: applied a temporary block to the maintenance job to prevent further mass invalidation: `scheduler disable-job --name cache-evict-euw1 --until 2026-03-12T10:00:00Z`.
Nia S.: good. customer impact: two enterprise integrations reported 10-30% elevated error rates for 5-12 minutes. CS will prepare customer note.
Marcus H.: we also pushed a targeted hotfix to the embedding worker which adds backoff after cache-miss storms. Deploy was at 09:18Z.
Taylor G.: rolling verification: error rates dropped after soft limiter and hotfix; latency back to baseline by 09:22Z. Still monitoring for recurrence.
ops-bot: Incident declared triaged by Taylor G. at 2026-03-12T09:15:00Z.
Nia S.: can someone draft a short internal status blurb for Slack and the status page? Keep it precise.
Taylor G.: internal status blurb for Slack/status page draft:
``
Incident: transient 429/timeout errors for embeddings in eu-west-1
Start: 2026-03-12 09:11:23 UTC
Mitigation: Temporarily increased soft rate-limits and blocked a maintenance job that triggered mass cache invalidation. Deployed worker backoff hotfix.
Impact: Short-lived elevated 429s and latency for some customers between 09:11 and 09:22 UTC.
Status: Resolved — monitoring. No data loss. Customer-facing summary to be sent to affected accounts.
``
Marcus H.: for the public status page please avoid technical root-cause details; something like "a maintenance job caused excessive cache churn" instead of implementation specifics.
Taylor G.: good point. customer-facing email draft for impacted customers (CS/Legal review required):
---
Subject: Brief service disruption affecting embeddings in eu-west-1 (Mar 12)
Hi <Customer>,
We want to follow up about a brief service disruption that affected embeddings requests in region eu-west-1 on Mar 12. During a routine maintenance job, cached data in our inference layer was invalidated more broadly than intended, which caused a short window of elevated errors and increased latency for some requests.
What we did:
- Immediately throttled incoming embedding requests and increased worker concurrency to stabilize throughput.
- Disabled the maintenance job that caused the mass invalidation.
- Deployed a backoff hotfix to reduce retries during cache warmup.
Impact:
- Some requests experienced 429 errors or higher latency between 09:11 and 09:22 UTC.
- We did not observe any data corruption or loss.
Next steps / preventative measures:
- Adding a safe-guard to maintenance job scheduling to prevent simultaneous invalidations across many hosts.
- Introducing a coordinated cache-warmup sequence so replicas rehydrate gradually rather than all at once.
- Updating our monitoring to detect cache-churn patterns and auto-mitigate earlier.
If you want a tailored timeline for your integration or would like to join an engineering call, please reply and we'll schedule time.
Thanks for your patience,
Nia Shah
Customer Success 1D Redwood Inference
---
Taylor G.: Legal asked to soften the phrase "maintenance job" to "internal cache maintenance task" — will update before send.
Nia S.: append an engineering appendix for customers who request it. Marcus, can you include the CLI commands and exact timestamps?
Marcus H.: appendix (engineering detail):
``
09:11:23 UTC - Alert: spike in 429s and timeouts on embeddings in eu-west-1
09:12:41 UTC - Soft rate-limiter increased: `infractl set-rate-limit --service embeddings --region eu-west-1 --soft 2000`
09:13:05 UTC - Maintenance job disabled: `scheduler disable-job --name cache-evict-euw1 --until 2026-03-12T10:00:00Z`
09:18:03 UTC - Hotfix deploy to embedding workers with backoff: `deployctl promote hotfix/emb-backoff --region eu-west-1`
09:22:10 UTC - Error rates returned to baseline; monitoring window started.
``
Luis M.: action items: (1) infra to add maintenance job safety checks (owner @luis.m) (2) eng-runtime to implement staggered cache-warmup (owner @marcus.h) (3) CS to send customer note and track replies (owner @nia.s). Owners confirm please.
Luis M.: confirmed. will open infra ticket and add runbook notes.
Marcus H.: confirmed, creating an RFC for staggered warmup and will link to incident.
Nia S.: confirmed; target send time for customer note: Mar 13 08:00 UTC after legal signoff. Will paste final sent copy here.
